findings.criterion: The UI strictly implements the parchment (#FDFBF7), charcoal (#1C1A17), and brass (#A38A5E) color palette with serif headers and sans-serif body text.
findings.evidence: styles.css defines --parchment: #FDFBF7, --charcoal: #1C1A17, and --brass: #A38A5E, along with --font-serif and --font-sans. These are applied to body, headers, and borders throughout the stylesheet.

findings.criterion: Users can add new decision options and view them in a structured, responsive layout.
findings.evidence: index.html contains the option-form and options-grid. app.js handles the submit event to push new options to the state and render them. The browser journey successfully executed the creation of 'Project Omega' and verified its presence.

findings.criterion: Users can delete decision options with an explicit confirmation dialog.
findings.evidence: app.js implements a click listener on '.btn-delete-card' which triggers a standard browser `confirm` dialog before filtering the option out of the state and saving.

findings.criterion: The application initializes with at least three default criteria for scoring.
findings.evidence: app.js initializes the criteria state with ['Impact', 'Feasibility', 'Alignment'] and renders them dynamically on load.

findings.criterion: The layout is fully responsive and keyboard-navigable.
findings.evidence: styles.css includes a media query at 1024px to stack the triptych-container columns vertically on smaller screens. Standard HTML form elements and buttons are used to ensure keyboard focusability.
